chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Qasim al-Kufi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a woman who gifted herself to a man from the Muslims, he said: 'If he were to offset it (with a payment), so that would be straight (correct)'.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling if a woman gifts herself to a man in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'hibat al-nafs' (gift of oneself) in Shia jurisprudence, establishing that a woman’s voluntary gift of herself to a man is legally binding provided he offers appropriate compensation (iwad). It highlights the flexibility of marital contracts in early Shia legal theory, distinguishing this voluntary gift from standard dowry (mahr) requirements while affirming the necessity of mutual consideration to validate the union.
